claim.summary: src/click/formatting.py holds click's help-text layout code. It has a module-level FORCED_WIDTH override, the helpers measure_table, iter_rows, wrap_text and join_options, and the in-memory HelpFormatter class. HelpFormatter accumulates strings in a buffer and tracks the current indent. It provides write_usage, write_heading, write_text, write_dl, the section and indentation context managers, and getvalue. Width is measured with term_len, which ignores ANSI escapes. wrap_text delegates to click._textwrap.TextWrapper, which I did not read. Command.format_help and Group.format_help in core.py create the formatter through Context.make_formatter, which uses Context.formatter_class (core.py:315, 638-649).

interfaces.name: wrap_text
interfaces.behavior:
wrap_text(text, width=78, initial_indent='', subsequent_indent='', preserve_paragraphs=False) -> str. It calls text.expandtabs() first, then builds a click._textwrap.TextWrapper with replace_whitespace=False. Without preserve_paragraphs it returns wrapper.fill(text). With preserve_paragraphs it splits text.splitlines() into paragraphs at empty lines. The first line's leading indent (measured with term_len) is recorded per paragraph and re-applied through wrapper.extra_indent. Lines within a paragraph are joined with spaces. If a paragraph's first line is only ' ' (checked with strip()), the marker line is dropped and the remaining lines are kept verbatim through wrapper.indent_only, joined with '
'. Paragraphs are joined with '

'. Since 8.4.0, width ignores ANSI escapes.
edge_cases: Empty text returns '' without the initial_indent, which is why write_usage special-cases empty args.
A single leading '\b' paragraph keeps its line breaks and indentation.
Tabs are expanded to 8-column stops.
Styled long words are broken between visible characters (test_wrap_text_visible_width).

interfaces.name: measure_table
interfaces.behavior: Takes an iterable of row tuples and returns a tuple of the maximum term_len for each column index, ordered by column index.
edge_cases: An empty rows iterable returns ().
Rows of differing length are measured per index.

interfaces.name: iter_rows
interfaces.behavior: Generator that pads each row tuple with empty strings up to col_count. It does `row + ('',) * (col_count - len(row))`.
edge_cases: A row longer than col_count is yielded unchanged.
rows must contain tuples, because a list row would fail on tuple concatenation.

interfaces.name: join_options
interfaces.behavior: Takes option strings and returns (', '.join(sorted opts), any_prefix_is_slash). The prefix of each option comes from parser._split_opt(opt)[0]. Options are stably sorted by prefix length, so '-v' comes before '--verbose'. The flag is True if any prefix is exactly '/'.
edge_cases: An empty iterable returns ('', False).
Options with equal prefix length keep their input order.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter
interfaces.behavior: HelpFormatter(indent_increment=2, width=None, max_width=None). max_width defaults to 80. If width is None it uses FORCED_WIDTH when set. Otherwise it uses max(min(shutil.get_terminal_size().columns, max_width) - 2, 50). Attributes are indent_increment, width, current_indent (starts at 0) and buffer (a list of str). Output is always in memory.
edge_cases: The computed width has a floor of 50.
An explicit width is used as given, with no clamp.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.write
interfaces.behavior: Appends the string to self.buffer with no processing. All other write_* methods go through it, so overriding it intercepts everything.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.indent
edge_cases: There is no lower bound check.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.dedent
edge_cases: It can go negative if unbalanced.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.write_usage
interfaces.behavior:
write_usage(prog, args='', prefix=None). The default prefix is _('Usage:') + ' '. It builds usage_prefix = f'{prefix:>{current_indent}}{prog} '. With empty args it writes usage_prefix.rstrip(' ') and '
' and returns. Otherwise, if width - current_indent >= term_len(usage_prefix) + 20, it writes wrap_text(args) with initial_indent=usage_prefix and a subsequent indent of spaces matching the prefix width. If not, it writes the prefix, then '
', then args wrapped with an indent of max(current_indent, term_len(prefix)) + 4. Both non-empty branches end with '
'.
edge_cases: Empty args gives 'Usage: prog\n' with no trailing space.
A styled prefix is measured with term_len.
The prefix is right-aligned to current_indent, so a prefix longer than the indent is not padded.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.write_heading
interfaces.behavior: Writes f"{'':>{current_indent}}{heading}:\n". A colon is always appended.
edge_cases: A heading that already ends in ':' gets a double colon.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.write_paragraph
interfaces.behavior: Writes '\n' only if the buffer is non-empty. This avoids a leading blank line.
edge_cases: It does nothing on a fresh formatter.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.write_text
interfaces.behavior: Wraps text with wrap_text(text, self.width, initial_indent and subsequent_indent set to ' ' * current_indent, preserve_paragraphs=True), then writes '\n'. The result honors the '\b' no-rewrap marker.
edge_cases: Empty text writes only '\n'.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.write_dl
interfaces.behavior: write_dl(rows, col_max=30, col_spacing=2). The rows are materialised into a list. The first column width is min(widest term, col_max) + col_spacing. Each term is written at current_indent. If the term is empty-valued (second is empty) only a newline follows. If term_len(first) fits within first_col - col_spacing, it is padded to the column. Otherwise the description goes on the next line, indented first_col + current_indent. The description is wrapped with wrap_text(second, max(width - first_col - 2, 10), preserve_paragraphs=True). The first wrapped line follows the term, and the continuation lines are indented by first_col + current_indent.
edge_cases: Rows with a length other than 2 (including an empty rows list) raise TypeError.
Short rows are padded via iter_rows.
A second value that wraps to no lines writes '\n'.
The text width has a floor of 10.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.section
interfaces.behavior: Context manager that calls write_paragraph, then write_heading(name), then indent(). It yields, and dedent() runs in a finally block.
edge_cases: Dedent is guaranteed even if the body raises.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.indentation
interfaces.behavior: Context manager that calls indent(), yields, then calls dedent() in a finally block.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.getvalue
edge_cases: Returns '' if nothing has been written.

interfaces.name: FORCED_WIDTH
interfaces.behavior: Module-level `int | None`, default None. HelpFormatter.__init__ reads it when width is None. testing.py sets it to 80 during CliRunner isolation (testing.py:437-438) and restores it afterwards (testing.py:592).
edge_cases: It is read at construction time only.

claim.error_conventions: The only exception raised directly is TypeError("Expected two columns for definition list") in HelpFormatter.write_dl. The message is a short sentence in capitalized style, with no trailing period and no values interpolated. Nothing else validates its input. The user-facing 'Usage:' string goes through gettext (`_`).

examples.description: HelpFormatter.write_text at a fixed width and indent
examples.code:
formatter = click.HelpFormatter(width=len("  Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet,"))
formatter.current_indent = 2
formatter.write_text(text)
actual = formatter.getvalue()
assert actual == "  Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet,\n  consectetur adipiscing elit\n"

examples.description: Styled usage prefix is measured by visible width
examples.code:
formatter = click.HelpFormatter(width=40)
formatter.write_usage("cli", "[OPTIONS]", prefix=styled_prefix)
visible = strip_ansi(formatter.getvalue())
assert visible == "Usage: cli [OPTIONS]\n"

examples.description: wrap_text with ANSI input compared with the stripped equivalent
examples.code:
styled = click.formatting.wrap_text(body, width=width, initial_indent=initial_indent)
plain = click.formatting.wrap_text(strip_ansi(body), width=width, initial_indent=strip_ansi(initial_indent))
assert [strip_ansi(l) for l in styled.splitlines()] == plain.splitlines()

examples.description: End-to-end help output at a forced terminal width
examples.code:
result = runner.invoke(cli, ["--help"], terminal_width=60)
assert result.output.splitlines() == ["Usage: cli [OPTIONS]", "", "  First paragraph.", ...]

tests.how_it_asserts: Plain pytest functions using the `runner` fixture. They call runner.invoke(cli, ['--help'], terminal_width=N) and compare result.output.splitlines() to an exact list of lines. Direct unit tests build click.HelpFormatter(...) and compare getvalue() to an exact string. The ANSI tests are parametrized with pytest.param(..., id=...), and they compare strip_ansi output of styled input against plain input. They cover wrapping of long usage lines, '\b' paragraphs, empty-args usage, docstring truncation and usage errors.

extension_points.name: Context.formatter_class
extension_points.what_could_attach: Set formatter_class to a HelpFormatter subclass (for example one that overrides write_dl, write_usage or write_heading) so every command renders with it. Context.make_formatter (core.py:638-649) instantiates it with width=terminal_width and max_width=max_content_width.

extension_points.name: HelpFormatter.write
extension_points.what_could_attach: Override to post-process or style every chunk, or to stream the output instead of buffering it.

extension_points.name: HelpFormatter.write_dl col_max and col_spacing
extension_points.what_could_attach: Subclasses can change the column layout, for example a different col_max, or extra columns beyond two.

extension_points.name: FORCED_WIDTH
extension_points.what_could_attach: Module-level override of the default width, used by the testing runner.

gaps.description: write_dl accepts only two columns, so a three-column table (for example option, default and description) is not possible.
gaps.why_plausible: measure_table and iter_rows are already generic over any number of columns. Only the `len(widths) != 2` check restricts write_dl.

gaps.description: Hanging-indent or bullet-list text helpers. Only write_text with the '\b' marker preserves layout.
gaps.why_plausible: wrap_text already takes initial_indent and subsequent_indent separately, so a write_text variant exposing them is a small addition.

gaps.description: write_heading has no way to skip the colon or take a custom suffix.
gaps.why_plausible: The format string is hard-coded as heading plus ':'. A parameter would be a small change.

gaps.description: The max_width default of 80 and the minimum width of 50 are hard-coded, with no configuration.
gaps.why_plausible: Related constants such as col_max and col_spacing are already parameters on write_dl.

limitations: The formatter always buffers in memory.
Width is only handled for ANSI escapes via term_len. Wide CJK or emoji characters are not accounted for, as far as this module shows.
The '\b' no-rewrap marker only works with preserve_paragraphs=True, and only when it is the first line of a paragraph.
Help text is not translated here beyond the 'Usage:' string.
I did not read click/_textwrap.py or click._compat.term_len, so the wrapping details come from the tests and docstrings.
